summary: Mild frustration with repeated failure to resolve issue
detailed_context: Scott was attempting to enable Telegram device pairing through debug routes, encountering authentication and command mismatch issues. Poseidon provided technical analysis (identifying the Cloudflare Access requirement and command discrepancies between bot and admin UI) but ultimately failed to deliver a working solution. Scott's terse "not working" indicates frustration after multiple attempted workarounds. The root cause is Poseidon's inability to actually resolve the underlying problem—while the technical diagnosis was sound, the proposed solutions (trying different policies, adding quick routes) apparently didn't execute successfully or weren't applicable. Scott likely expected either a functional workaround or clear next steps, not just problem identification. This reveals Scott values actionable solutions over technical explanations when troubleshooting; repeated diagnosis without resolution erodes confidence. Poseidon should have either: (1) provided a verified working solution before suggesting it, (2) admitted the blocker upfront, or (3) offered genuinely alternative approaches with higher success probability rather than theoretical fixes.
